messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU capacity exhausted in us-west-2 (pool: general-gpu). autoscaler attempted scale but hit provider quota/scale limit. queue growth > 3k, p95 latency +1200ms. paging oncall team now.

sam: saw the page, on it. starting quick triage — `kubectl get pods -n inference | grep general-gpu`

nina: hitting this too, can confirm large queue backlog on the reconcile queue. backlog metric `inference.queue.pending{pool=\"general-gpu\"}` spiked ~00:45 UTC.

lee: @sam @nina are we getting provider 429s or scaleError from autoscaler?

sam: logs show repeated scale errors: `ScaleUp failed: quota_exceeded` from provider API. also autoscaler marked nodes NotReady during drain attempts (oom?). past 10m we saw 429s on provisioning endpoint.

emily: customer impact: CS reports ~12 customers seeing timeouts for inference calls between 00:42-01:05 UTC. some requests got 503, others queued > 30s. I'm patching status page.

mike: temporary mitigation ideas: 1) divert low-pri tenants to warm-dedicated pool, 2) enable emergency-throttle on public API, 3) manual scale override if provider allows.

sam: doing (1) now — adding routing rule to move tenants tagged `prio:low` to `dedicated-warm-02`. applying policy: `route-match: tenant.prio==low -> model_pool=dedicated-warm-02`.

nina: routing applied, I see traffic drop on general-gpu for low tenants. queue size decreased ~12% in first 2 mins.

lee: trying (2) — toggling emergency rate limit. `POST /admin/limits` with body `{\n  \"global_tokens_per_minute\": 200000,\n  \"throttle_policy\": \"gradual_drop\"\n}`

infra_bot: action: emergency throttle enabled by lee at 00:50 UTC.

sam: provider team responded: quota increase delayed 30–45m. they offered transient preemptible capacity but needs manual acceptance.

mike: I'll accept preemptible nodes to relieve immediate backlog. doing manual add: `infractl provider add-nodes --region us-west-2 --type p3-preemptible --count 8`

infra_bot: provider add-nodes request submitted (req-9042). estimated ready in ~4m.

emily: CS update: informing affected customers that mitigation in progress, ETA ~10m. watching for errors.

sam: preemptible nodes came up @00:54. autoscaling metrics show capacity increased; queue drained to under 600 in 6m. latency back to normal for most tenants.

nina: note: some inference workers logged `kv-cache OOM` after nodes joined — looks like a shader/driver mismatch causing worker restarts. we've isolated to model-serving-runtime v1.9.2 on preemptible image.

lee: rolling back model-serving-runtime to v1.9.1 on those nodes. `kubectl set image daemonset/serving runtime=runtime:v1.9.1 -n inference --record`

sam: roll completed, restarts stabilized. no further OOMs.

emily: monitoring shows customer error rate reduced to baseline. I'm moving status to "degraded -> mitigated".

mike: summary of live mitigations: 1) routed low-priority tenants to warm-dedicated pool, 2) emergency global throttling enabled, 3) accepted preemptible nodes, 4) rolled runtime on new nodes to stable version.

cs_lead: CS: created ticket to affected customers with full timeline + credits. good job on rapid mitigation.

incident-bot: INCIDENT annotated: severity=high, impacted_customers=12+, start=6189991234, mitigated=6189993640.

sam: quick postmortem notes (will draft full later):
- root cause: provider quota exhaustion + autoscaler not failing over to fallback pool when scale attempts returned quota errors.
- contributing: routing policy had low-pri tenants colocated in same pool; emergency throttle alert thresholds were too permissive (fired late).
- immediate fix applied: manual routing + preemptible capacity + rollback runtime.

nina: initial action items (short):
- A1: add autoscaler fallback to route to dedicated-warm pools on quota errors (owner: infra, due: 7d).
- A2: add alert that triggers when `provider.scale_errors > 3` within 5m (owner: eng-runtime, due: 3d).
- A3: validate images for preemptible node types via canary tests (owner: eng-ml, due: 5d).

lee: ops items:
- O1: update emergency throttle runbook with exact API steps + rollback (owner: eng-oncall, due: 2d).
- O2: pre-approve provider transient capacity window with vendor (owner: infra + finance, due: 14d).

mike: infra cleanup:
- I1: remove preemptible nodes or convert to reserved if vendor confirms sustained capacity (owner: infra, due: 1d).
- I2: add a small warm buffer capacity for peak windows (owner: infra, due: 14d).

emily: customers:
- C1: CS to send post-incident summary and apply credits (owner: cs_lead, due: 1d).

sam: draft follow-up doc: I'll capture metrics graphs (queue size, latency, scale error rate), exact timestamps, and attach logs. aiming to post full postmortem to #postmortems by EOD tomorrow.

nina: also suggest we add a regression test that simulates provider 429s to ensure autoscaler fallback works in staging. (owner: eng-runtime, due: 7d)

cs_lead: flag for product: check if any SLA commitments were breached for affected customers and whether credit thresholds require escalation.

sam: closing live thread. marking incident as mitigated. will reopen if we see reoccur. thanks all. :hands_together:

incident-bot: Incident status updated to MITIGATED by sam at 6189993640.
